utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yesterday we left to reflect on the issue which was debated before us and on which we subsequently received written submissions, and following lengthy deliberations on the matter, the Trial Chamber has decided unanimously to refuse to admit the evidence of the Witness K-82. The reasons for that determination will be explained in a written decision which will be published as soon as possible and certainly before the end of next week. Now, Mr. Stamp, who is the next witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: The next witness -- [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: -- Isa Raka who will be taken by Ms. Daniela Kravetz, who is now in court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And this witness gives evidence in what form?

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Your Honour, we had initially submitted this witness's evidence pursuant to 92 bis (B). When he was here in proofing some weeks ago, he provided additional information, and we have now prepared an 89(F) statement which was disclosed to the Defence on 8 September. So we would like to proceed with this witness today pursuant to 89(F).

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Very well. Let's have the witness brought in, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Your Honour, while this witness is brought in, I would like to point out that there are two minor typos in this witness's 89(F) statement. There is incorrect numbering of the paragraphs. The paragraph numbering jumps from number 15 to 17. There is no paragraph 16 missing; it's just been incorrectly numbered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And also I presume in the English version you would have noted that the witness's gender has been incorrectly noted as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. And just I think for completeness, give us, please, the paragraphs of the indictment to which this evidence relates.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Yes. The evidence of this witness primarily refers to paragraph 72(k), 73, 75(k) and paragraph 76 and 77. He speaks about events that took place in the municipality of Kacanik.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Raka.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Would you now please make the solemn declaration to tell the truth, by reading aloud the document which will be placed before you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Please be seated. Mr. Raka, we have before us a written statement of your evidence. The purpose of you being here today is so that questions can be asked, some of them to clarify, some to add to, and others to challenge what is already in your statement. Please remember we have this statement before us, we've all read it, and therefore the important thing is to concentrate on the particular point that is raised with you in each question. Listen carefully to each question and try to confine your answer to the particular point that is raised with you in that question. The first person to ask questions of you will be for the Prosecution, Ms. Kravetz. Ms. Kravetz.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Witness, please state your full name for the record?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: Isa Raka.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: I understand from your statement that you were born in the village -- in the town of Kacanik?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And is it where you have been living all your life?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Mr. Raka, in November of 1999, did you provide a statement to representatives of the Office of the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And have you recently had the chance to go over this statement with representatives of the OTP?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: In the course of doing so, did you provide additional information and clarify some aspects of your statement?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: Yes. Some minor things.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Could the witness please be provided a hard copy of his statement?

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Mr. Raka, the statement before you is in English. I understand you speak a little English. I would just like you to look at it and tell me if you recognise the statement.

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And do you recognise your signature on this statement?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Was this statement read back to you in Albanian by an interpreter?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And are you satisfied that what was read out to you properly and accurately reflects the changes you wanted to make to your previous statement?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And Mr. Raka, does this statement accurately reflect to the best of your knowledge and recollection the truth of the events that are described in the statement?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: Yes. To my knowledge and conviction, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: I would like at this time to tender the statement. It's Exhibit P2301.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Mr. Raka, it has been explained to you here, this statement is in evidence before the Court. I would like to ask you some questions and briefly go over some aspects of this statement with you. Yes, in paragraph 8 of your statement, you describe that between the 24th and 27th of March, there was -- the police in Kacanik began shooting from the police station. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Is this something that you were personally able to observe?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: I didn't see that with my own eyes but we heard the shots coming from the police station.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: You heard the shots coming from the police station? From where? Where were you at the time?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: We could hear them from our house. From the house of my uncle, actually.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And during these days from the 24th to the 27th of March, how frequently would you hear this shooting from the police station?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: Very frequently, especially during the night. They were continuous during night.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And what did you and your family do when you realised this was happening in the town, this shooting was going on?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: During the day, we stayed at home. At night we went to stay with my uncle's people.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And where was your uncle's house located in relation to your house?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: His house is 100 metres away, as a crow flies, maximum 150.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Okay. Mr. Raka, in paragraph 11 of your statement you state that early on 27 March, you saw firing with a rocket launcher against the house of Shaip Dema. Excuse my pronunciation; I am not sure it's correct.

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. And you pronounced the name correctly.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: From where were you able to observe this firing?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: I saw it from my own house.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And from which direction was the firing coming?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: The shooting was coming from the police station.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And do you recall approximately how many rounds were fired against the house of Shaip Dema?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: Six times.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Where was the house of Shaip Dema located in relation to your house? Was it in your same neighbourhood?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: No. It is in Bob village, but the Bob village is across the place where my house is situated.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: What do you mean that it's across the place where your house is situated?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: I mean that it is very easily for me from my house to see what's going on in the Bob village.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Okay. And who was occupying the house of Shaip Dema prior to this date when the firing started?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: Before this date when -- before the firing started, it was the OSCE that was stationed there.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Mr. Raka, you told us that you were able to see this shooting on the morning of 27 March. Did you at any time that morning leave your house?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: No. We did not leave the house that morning. In the morning, we returned home. As I said, during the night we went to my uncle's house.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And on 27 March, you were at your home. Did you at any time maybe later during the day visit one of your neighbours?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: Yes. I visited the house of Jakup Jakupi.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: While you were at your neighbour's house, were you able to observe anything unusual happening in Kacanik?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: What were you able to observe happening?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: I saw two military jeeps and a Niva car entering the lime factory.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: You say you saw two military jeeps entering the lime factory. Where was the lime factory located in relation to your house?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: The lime factory is on the other side of the Lepence village -- river, correction. It's about 100 metres away from where my house is.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: So it's directly opposite the river from your house?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: You stated that you saw two jeeps arriving to the lime factory. And who was in those jeeps?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: In the jeeps were about 20 policemen wearing green -- blue, correction, camouflage uniforms and two were wearing green camouflage uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And when the policemen arrived to the lime factory were you able to observe what they did there?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: They got off the jeeps and one of them, whom I took to be Lubisha and I was certain it was him, they were making signs with their hands as if ordering people to do something, ordering their policemen to do something.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: You mention a man called Lubisha. Who was Lubisha? What position did he occupy?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: From the information I received, he was deputy commander, I think, of the police station.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Did you know him prior to this date? Had you seen him on any other occasion?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. I knew him.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: How did you know him?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: I knew him because he lived in the same neighbourhood with me, some 100 metres away from my house.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: So you said you saw Lubisha giving orders to the other policemen. What exactly were the other policemen doing at the factory?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: Policemen, some of them were crawling, some were walking, towards the factory. They circled round the factory and then they took up positions there.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Was the factory empty at the time? Was it closed?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: Yes. There were only the guards.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And what happened after the policemen took positions in the factory? What were you able to observe happen?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: Once they took up their positions, they started to fire randomly.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: You say they were firing. Do you know in which direction they were firing?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: Yes. They fired in the direction of the houses.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: When you say fire in the direction of the houses, you mean the houses in your area of town?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And was there anyone firing from your area of town towards the factory?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would like to show the witness some photographs at this stage. This is Exhibit 2310. These photographs are not on our exhibit list. They were provided by the witness to the Prosecution, and I would like to apply to have these photographs added and to be allowed to show them to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Is there any objection to that?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. By your leave, the aforementioned photographs were not on the exhibit list that accompanied the testimony of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, we've been told by Ms. Kravetz that they were not on the exhibit list, which is I presume is the 65 ter list.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: They were included in the updated version of the witness's notification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And the explanation is that he provided them to the Prosecution. So that's been conceded. So you object to them being produced, do you?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understood, Your Honour. But up until this moment, we haven't had an opportunity that this will be tendered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Did you receive a copy of them?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Your Honour, I understand the Defence has been provided copies. They were provided copies last week, and in the updated notification, which was filed on 14th November, the photographs appeared listed as one of the exhibits to be used through this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And they are plainly in the library of the e-court system because they have a number, P2310.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: They are, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Do you maintain your objection, Mr. Cepic?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I withdraw my objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Very well. You can put them to the witness. Are you seeking to use e-court for this?

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Yes, I have it right here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Could we zoom in on the photograph with ERN ending 3167? It's that one.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Mr. Raka, do you have these photographs on your screen? Do they appear on your screen?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Could you tell us what is depicted in the photograph to the right of your screen, the first photograph to the right?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: This photo depicts the place where the police were positioned.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Is this the lime factory you spoke about earlier?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: You said you saw the police arriving in two jeeps. Could you tell us where you saw them on this photograph?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: Here, on this part.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Could you mark that with an X maybe?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: In this part here.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And you said you saw the policemen take up positions where they started firing from. Could you put a circle around where you saw them take up positions?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: The police positions were here, at these windows, and were those two soldiers came after five minutes took up these positions here.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Mr. Raka, this structure we see here, this sort of tower we see here at the factory, is this one of the highest points in this area of town?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: It probably is, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: For clarification of the record, the lowest red mark on the photograph shows where the jeeps arrived. The two higher marks show positions from which firing emerged.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Could we zoom in on the photograph with ERN --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You can't move now without losing what you've got.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Yes, could we take a snapshot of this and have this exhibit be assigned a following IC number?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be IC38, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Could we now move to the photograph with ERN ending in 3169?

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Mr. Raka, could you tell us what is depicted on this photograph?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: In this photograph, you can see my house and the house I was at the moment when the firing started.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Could you mark a 1 next to your house?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And could you put a 2 next to the house where you were observing what was happening at the lime factory?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Thank you. From where is this photograph taken, Mr. Raka?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: I took the photos in order to explain more clearly the positions where the police were and where my house was and where I was staying.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: So this photograph was taken from the positions you marked with a circle on the previous photograph, where the police was stationed?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Raka, when did you take these photographs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I took these photographs sometime in 2002.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Could we now zoom in on the third photographs one is ERN ending in 3168 -- oh, a snapshot, please, of this, yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This one will be, Your Honours, IC39.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Mr. Raka, could you tell us what we see on this third photograph?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: We see the position from where I observed what was going on.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And is this roof that we see on the right-hand side of the photograph the roof of your house?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: It is the courtyard of my neighbour.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Mr. Raka, moving on now, you said the police was firing from these positions. For approximately how long were they firing towards your area of town?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: The fire lasted approximately some 30 minutes or more.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And do you know if any people, anyone resulted injured as a result of this firing, of this shooting?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: Yes. My wife got injured.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Where was your wife when she was injured?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: My wife was at home.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And do you know how she got injured?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: She got injured because of the shots.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And where exactly in the house was she at the time she was injured?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: She was in the cellar.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Your wife was injured while she was in the cellar, or was she at some point trying to leave the cellar when she was injured?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: At the moment when the firing started, she tried to go from one cellar to a next cellar where she felt she was safer.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And where was she at the time she was injured?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: At the moment when she was leaving the cellar. She was in the yard, I would say.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Mr. Raka, after the firing or the shooting ended, were you able to return to your house?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: No. We left the house. I went back. I got my injured wife and together we left.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And were you able to obtain medical attention for your wife?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: No. About after some ten hours, a doctor came and gave her some blood.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And did you try to take your wife to the local hospital in Kacanik for medical attention?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: It was impossible to do that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Why was it impossible to do that at the time?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: Because of the war situation.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: You said you left your house and that later your wife received medical attention. Did you later decide to leave Kacanik?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Did you leave alone with your family or were others with you at the time?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: The entire neighbourhood.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And could you explain why the neighbourhood was leaving, why your neighbours were also leaving the town?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: They were leaving because we heard that the police entered a house and got three people from there, one of them they killed. This made us leave the houses.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: You said you heard the police had taken some people from a house. From whom did you hear this?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: We heard this from the people in the neighbourhood, the people who were closer to the place where the police went.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And were these people also leaving the town?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: Yes, yes, all of them.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Approximately how many of you were in this group with you leaving the town that day?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: We were, I would say, about 1.000. I might say from 500 to 1.000.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And in which direction did you led when you left the town of Kacanik?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: We went in the direction of Gjurgjedol.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: How long did you remain once you arrived to this town Gjurgjedol? How long did you remain there?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: We stayed there one night.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And where did you continue after you left that location?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: We continued our way towards Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Were you able to cross a border into Macedonia, Mr. Raka?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: Not the first time.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And when were you able to cross the border?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: Not -- not even the second time. It was only the third time that we managed to cross the border to Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: So how many days were you waiting to cross a border into Macedonia?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: From the moment that my wife was wounded until we reached Macedonia, it took us two days. At the border we waited some three, four, five hours, and the house -- the army stopped us two times.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Once you crossed the border into Macedonia, were you able to obtain medical assistance for your wife?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: Yes. I took her to the hospital of Skopje.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And was she able to recover from her injuries, the injuries she had sustained that day of the shooting?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: No. No. She was not. She died.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: How old was your wife, Mr. Raka, when she died?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: She was born in 1971. At that time she was 27 years old or 28 years old.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And was she pregnant at the time she was injured?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: Yes, she was.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I have a moment?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Raka, can I just ask you one thing? The lime factory, when you took the photographs in 2002, was it operational, operating as a lime factory?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Preparations were underway to start operation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And when the events took place in March 1999, was it operating then as a lime factory?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't remember very well, but I know that there were guards 24 hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And what about today? Does it function today?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have no further questions of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. O'Sullivan?

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, the order will be General Lukic, General Pavkovic, General Lazarevic, Mr. Sainovic, Mr. Milutinovic and General Ojdanic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Mr. Raka. I'm Branko Lukic, and together with my colleagues Dragan Ivetic and Ozren Ogrizovic, we represent General Lukic. Do you have your statement in Albanian, and do you need it if you don't have it?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: No, I don't have it in Albanian. I have it in English. If possible, I would really appreciate having the Albanian version before me.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Could we go to paragraph 7 immediately, please? You say there were only civilians in the house. "No one from our family was in the KLA."

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know that in the village of Bob, there were some 400 members of the KLA?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: Up until that time, the 27th of March, there wasn't. At least I don't know that there was.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know that in the neighbouring forests and on the hilltops, there were members of the KLA?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now I would like you to go to paragraph 8, please. You say here that between 24 and 27 March 1999, there was shooting from the police station in Kacanik. They were shooting without any specific target. I believe that the witness said yes but it has not been reflected in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, we can assume it because you're simply reading his statement to him. So please carry on to the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Since you lived in Kacanik, do you know that the police station in Stari Kacanik came under attack on the 27th of March, 1999, at 1850?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: I don't know. Kacanik i Vjeter to my knowledge is a village.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: How far away is Stari Kacanik from your house?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: I don't know exactly because I've never been there. I have no family there.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Very well. Do you know that on that same day, the 27 March 1999, in Bob village, a column of the Yugoslav army was attacked sometime between 1600 and 1700 hours, and that the attack came from the lime factory, precisely from there?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But you said that on that day, you were observing what was going on in the lime factory. How come you didn't see one incident and you saw the other?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: On the 27th March, around the time you mentioned, I was at my uncle's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And from your uncle's house, were you able to see this incident?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: No. It cannot be observed from there.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Very well. Can we now have Exhibit 2310 on e-court, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Before you move on to that, Mr. Raka, the -- you talked about random shooting from the police station in Kacanik between the 24th and the 27th. And you also talked in your statement about firing against the house of Shaip Dema in the village of Bob, and that was from the area of the police station. These two separate incidents, are you referring to the same police station?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] To my knowledge, it is the same police station. It's only one. And the firing towards Shaip Dema's house occurred in the morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Can we have the exhibit on e-court, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Raka, photo 3168, these are the last four digits of the photo, presents the place from which you were observing the events that you have described for us; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: This photograph was taken from the courtyard of my neighbour, not exactly from the window from where I was observing, just to show the position where I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In other words, none of these photos shows the view that you had while observing the developments that you've described?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: These photographs clearly show the event that I described.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I may have not been clear enough. I'll repeat. Is it correct that in no one of these three photos we can see the view that you yourself had when you were observing the event?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: Please be more clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'll try. Can you please point to the photo among the three that you see before you which depicts the view that you yourself had while you were observing the events that you have described for us, and which was taken from the place where were you standing while you were observing the event?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: This is the door to my neighbour's house, and here is a window. The window is marked with a spot, with a dot, and I was actually observing from this window. Not only me but the family of my neighbour was also observing.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: However, the photo that you are showing to us was taken from a different side and depicts the house where you were. And I'm asking you this: Neither 3168 nor 3167 depict or reflect the view that you had as you were looking towards the lime factory?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: Well, one can go to the very spot and verify this, what you're saying.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Could you please answer by just yes or no? Does any of the two upper photos show the view that you yourself had on the day when you were observing the events, just yes or no, please?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Which one? Which one is that?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: This is a position from the factory towards the house from where they were firing. Photograph 3168 shows the position minus or plus two metres from where I was observing. And photograph 3167, the position where the police stopped, where the police was.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In other words, if 3168 is the photo that depicts your view, then in no case could you observe the position of the police that you have described and marked in photo 3167, because that part of the lime factory you could not see from the position depicted in the photo 3168.

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: We could see it because when the police were taking up positions and when they were climbing the staircase, we could see exactly where they were taking these positions.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Remember the view from 3168, and we shall now go to Exhibit IC38, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Do you wish this one captured for posterity?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour, no. It doesn't mean anything. [In English] It means nothing, Your Honour, because it doesn't show the view we are trying to establish here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: All right. No need to take that one. We'll move on. So can we have IC38?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you see now that the X that you put on photo 3167 could not be seen by you from the place that you showed to us in the photo 3168?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: I was very clear in my answer. In 3168, it is plus/minus two metres from the position where I was. I took this photograph from the staircase at my neighbour's house. We could see very clearly from this position, and you can verify if you go to the very spot in the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I would very much like to go there but we can't do that at the moment. That's why I'm asking you. Could you please tell us, then, where from did you take this photo, 3168? Where did you take it from?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: He's just told you he took it from the staircase of his neighbour's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: How is it possible, then, for you to climb two metres higher?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: The photograph was taken in 2002, as I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But that's not the answer to my question.

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: What do you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Were you on the staircase at the moment when the developments were taking place, the events that you described for us?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: I was very clear in my answer. This photograph was taken in 2002, and it was not taken from the position where I was observing. It was taken from my neighbour's courtyard, and you can see very clearly from the photograph where I was. The other photograph, not this one.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we then conclude that these photos are not of use to us and they can't help us understand what actually happened?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Is that a question to me? Which may be an appropriate person to pose it to. It's certainly not one to ask the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Just one thing you mayor clarify for me, Mr. Raka. We have certainly in the English translation a reference to you on a staircase. Was that when you were viewing the events in 1999 or was that when you were taking the photograph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When I was taking the photograph in 2002, I did that from the staircase of my neighbour's house; while on the 27th of March 1999, I went to my neighbour to ask for something, the police forces came, and then my neighbour offered me to go inside his house.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So you were viewing it from a window inside the house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: The photograph was taken from the courtyard outside?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, from outside.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can I move on, Your Honour? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You say that fire was opened from the police station by using a rocket launcher. Do you know what rocket launchers exactly?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: I don't know that because I'm not a military person. I did not complete my military service. But I know that there was shooting coming from the police station, shooting from a rocket launchers or whatever they called them.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You didn't see them firing from rocket launchers; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: No. I did see them when they fired at Shaip Dema's house. They fired six times.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You saw the police station at the moment when they opened fire on Shaip Dema's house?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: I didn't see it, but the shooting was coming from that direction.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So you don't know whether it was actually coming from the police station?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: It was coming from the centre, and the police station is in the centre of Kacanik.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Therefore, we can conclude that you didn't see fire being opened from the police station, isn't that so?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: The statement doesn't claim that he did. The statement is clearly to the effect the shooting was coming from the area of the police station.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The problem is it's not possible to fire a rocket launcher from the building. It would destroy the building itself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: We'll hear that, no doubt, in due course when you lead evidence. But the witness isn't saying it came from the building.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Okay, Your Honour. I move on. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In paragraph 8 you also state that curfew was introduced in the town. How were you notified of that?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: In fact, there was no movement in the town, along the asphalt road, because we couldn't see the city from that part. So it means that it was a curfew, because there was no movement at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Were you notified officially by radio or in any written form as to the introduction of that curfew?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: No, we were not officially informed by anyone, but the situation spoke for itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let us move on to paragraph 12, please. Can you please tell us again how many policemen came in front of the lime factory?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: I didn't count them, but I would say 20 to 30 policemen for sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And they all came in those three jeeps?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So seven to ten people per jeep, and those jeeps actually can seat four?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: Well, those who were actually on the jeep know better how they could go in that number in the jeep.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You mentioned Lubisha there. You say that your neighbour -- that he was your neighbour. What was he wearing at the time?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: What do you mean? When he came to the factory?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: He was wearing a police uniform, blue camouflage one. I was positive that it was him, at least from the position from where I was observing.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In paragraph 14, you state that he ordered the others to come out of the jeeps. What did the policemen do after that?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: Yes. They started to crawl, some of them crawled, some were walking on foot, around the factory. You can see this on 3167. They came out then in this part here.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In your statement, in paragraph 14, you state -- or, rather, you don't mention anyone walking but that they came out of the vehicles and started crawling. Were there some who walked as well?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: I was very clear. They were crawling, some of them were walking on foot.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Were they next to each other, some crawling, some walking?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: Yes. They were kind of together, in a group.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Isa, it is our Defence's position that your testimony in this part is illogical. There is a group of people, some of them walking, whereas others crawl. Do you still stand by that?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: They did not walk the way you think. They were walking faster and those that were crawling, they were crawling fast.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we conclude, then, that these policemen clearly sensed some danger, that they felt they were under threat?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: I don't think they were under threat. They wanted to cause fear among the population. This is at least what I think, why they were doing that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you recognise anyone else among the group?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: No. Except for Lubisha, who I believe was Lubisha, the one who was standing by the jeep.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And you didn't tell members of the ICG that you recognised Oliver, Brace, Tita, Bane, as well as someone who worked for the post office, this Bane?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: They could have been there as well, but how can I explain this now? I don't know about Bane, but the other policemen, I was told by other people that they were very strict. I could know them through other people, not personally.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you see whether the members of that unit had sniping rifles? Did you see them carrying snipers?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: I was convinced that they were firing from sniper rifles, and you can see the place where they were firing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I sense I may be treading on glass here, but your question about the ICG suggests a statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, it's his statement to the ICG.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Now are you saying that within that statement there is reference to recognising people?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: He mentioned those people.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, that's rather different, but it's just the way the question was framed and we are not seeing the statement. I want to be clear that the question has been put --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: He just explained us that it's not that he recognised those people.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: No, but are you claiming it that in the statement he said he recognised them?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: May I have a second, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The statement says names of perpetrators, Lubisha, Oliver, Brace, Tita, and Bane, former employee of the Kacanik post office. It's not clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: No, no. That's fine. Thank you, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Isa, did you know that those Albanians who were loyal to Serbia were often declared collaborators and were often targeted by the KLA?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: No, I don't know that. I have heard the word "collaborator" but I have not heard of cases like this.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that in fact, the two guards who worked for the factory which was owned by Serbia were actually killed by the KLA and that that was the reason why the police came?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: The two persons that were killed at the factory, they were working as guards in the factory.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We heard that from you earlier, and this is in your statement. I'm asking you this: Did you know that they were in fact killed by members of the KLA?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: That is not true, that they were killed by the KLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You are telling us in your statement that you don't know who killed them. How can you exclude the possibility I suggested, therefore?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: Based on what Halil's sons said, the picture 3168, the lower part, that's where the jeep with the two soldiers went, and most probably they killed them. Halid [phoen] and Shefket were sitting below there.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You saw all this?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: I didn't say that I saw that with my own eyes, but his sons saw that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In paragraph 18, you describe a gypsy who was walking along your side of the river and who was killed when the firing started. Was your wife wounded at approximately the same time?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. At approximately the same time.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: How much time elapsed until the moment when the gypsy's body was taken away?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: I don't know how much time elapsed, but I heard that somebody came and took his body.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You state that this someone who collected the body was also almost shot. Does that mean that within this one hour, the body was collected as well, or was it after the exchange of fire or, rather, the firing?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: Based on what I heard, the person who took the body was from the clinic nearby, from Kacanik, and I heard that he was stopped by the police on his way and nearly killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In your statement, you said that person was almost shot too. Is it your testimony today --

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: Very clear, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Please go on.

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: I told you that the person who came from the clinic to collect the body of the Roma, I heard that he was stopped by the police and that he was nearly killed, together with his driver.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know what ethnicity that person is, as well as the ethnicity of his driver?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: Based on the information that I have, he was Albanian. And in Kacanik, most of the drivers who worked at the clinic were Albanians.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So both the paramedic and the driver were Albanians employed with the health centre in Kacanik at the time of the firing; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: Only the driver came to collect the body. Now, I don't know whether he was a driver, a doctor or a nurse. This is what I heard, that only one person came to collect the body.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So the police didn't stop, as you previously stated, someone from the medical facility plus his driver, but rather they only stopped one single person? Is this what you are telling us now?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: I'm very clear. The person who came to collect the body of Jonuz on his way back to the clinic, I heard that he was stopped by the police, and that the driver of the clinic was nearly killed. Now, I don't know whether he was a driver or a doctor. This is what I heard. The body of Jonuz was carried by this personnel of the clinic, because when the body was collected, we had already left our house.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But in the meantime you called the health centre in Kacanik; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: My cousin, I don't know, he was lucky to get through because the phone was not working properly. Sometimes it worked, sometimes it didn't. I don't know now if he called the clinic or the house of the doctor, and he asked for help for my wife. This happened in late hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But that call took place during the firing, is that so?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: When the phone call was made, I don't think there was firing; at least there were scarce firing, sporadic firing.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Something is not clear to me. If someone came there with an ambulance to collect the dead gypsy, and since you say you gave that call to the health centre as well, why didn't they take your wife as well, but, rather, they sent a doctor to come from the other side, through the forest?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: At the time when they came to collect Jonuz's body, we were not here. I told you this. We had already left the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Where did you go after having left your house? You went to your neighbourhood, isn't that so?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: To my uncle's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: How far away is your uncle's house from your house?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: About ten, 15 minutes away. It is in the centre of the neighbourhood.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: How far away is the hospital from your house?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: It's not a hospital. It's a clinic. It's in the other part of the town. On foot, about half an hour, 20 to 30 minutes approximately. I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Therefore, you were told by the hospital that it was dangerous for you to come, but at the same time, they didn't refuse you. They didn't say that they wouldn't give you assistance; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: Something like that, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I have to state our position yet again. Our Defence believes that the people who were employed with the hospital were not afraid of the state authorities of Serbia but, rather, they were afraid of being attacked by KLA members. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: On the contrary. From what I heard, they were scared and afraid of the Serbian police, and as I mentioned, the case with the driver who was nearly killed by the Serbian police.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Serbian policemen, who could be wounded at any time and who could need medical assistance at any moment, in your view, presented a danger for the personnel at the health centre, is that your testimony?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: Can you repeat your question, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Is it your testimony today that Serbian armed forces presented a danger for those employed with the Serbian state hospitals?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: I was very clear, sir. The person who went to collect Jonuz's body and carried his body to the clinic, I heard that he was threatened by the Serb police, and this clearly shows that he was threatened by the police. This is what I heard.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Is this a suitable time to interrupt you?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, and I have only two or three questions, very short.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Very well. We'll resume at five past 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic. Oh, sorry, no witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Raka, do you know how far away is the Shaip house from the lime factory? And you said of that house that it had been hit by a rocket launcher.

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: Approximately from the pictures, I can show you from this photograph, in this photograph, where Shaip's house is. It's these houses here, uphill. It's -- you can see here the asphalt road, the main road, and somewhere here it's Shaip's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Could you give us a distance?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: Well, as the crow flies, but first of all tell me do you mean from the factory or from the police station?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The factory, the factory.

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: From the factory, approximately 250 metres or 300 metres. I can't tell you exactly, because Shaip's house is very close to the asphalt road, and it stood out because it was a nice house.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you hear in the meantime that Jonuz Berisha, the gypsy that you mentioned, is actually alive, that he was -- actually, that he was still alive when he was transported from Kacanik to Pristina?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: Maybe he was alive, but as I told you earlier, I did not see him. Maybe he was alive or he was dead. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let's briefly go back to this. Why did you go on that day from your house to your uncle's house, or your neighbour's house, I don't know?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: I went to my neighbour's house to borrow something. I can't even remember what I went there to borrow. I was asked by my family to go.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. On that day, did the police cross the river, from the factory towards your house?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And tell me, please, who was it who decided that people from your neighbourhood should set out towards Macedonia?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: Hamit's death, and Sefedin Beqa's sons who were taken away by the police, this is what caused us to leave. We were told by our neighbours, by the people who lived close to where these people lived, what had happened, and so people decided to leave.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: On page 15, line 24, my learned friend Kravetz asked you why you were not able to cross to Macedonia. Who was it who prevented you from crossing the border into Macedonia?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: What do you mean, where the Macedonian army stopped us or when the event happened, when we were not able to give any assistance? Could you clarify, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When you were on the border, who was it who stopped you from entering Macedonia, the first and the second time?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: We were prevented by the Macedonian forces. They were military forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. I have no further questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Lukic. Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Raka. I just -- I want to ask you about paragraph 12 of your statement, the last two sentences of that paragraph. You were talking about the police that came to that lime factory. You said two of the officers wore different uniforms, they wore regular army, VJ camouflage uniforms which have a green and brown pattern. Now by saying that, you certainly don't mean to suggest that they were actually members of the VJ but simply that they were wearing uniforms that looked the same as the VJ might wear. Correct?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: Well, the persons who were there know that. From what I was able to observe, they had green camouflage uniforms. I know that the police uniforms are blue camouflage, and these were different.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Yeah. But as far as you know, they were local Serbs dressed up in camouflage uniforms and not actually members of the army; correct? You don't know who they were, do you?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: No, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: That's all I have, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ackerman. Does that solve your problem too, Mr. Cepic?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Absolutely, Your Honour. Thank you very much, Your Honour, once again. We don't have any questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Fila?

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I will have a few questions for this witness, just to clear up some terminology. I would just like to check whether the witness understands what he's saying.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: I'm Toma Fila, I represent Nikola Sainovic. I'll -- I'm going to ask you some things in order to clear up some terminology. When the doctor arrived to examine your wife, in the statement, you said that he gave her an infusion, and today you said that he gave her a transfusion. Do you know the difference between an infusion and a transfusion, or maybe you can clarify what the doctor did. It would be very difficult to give a transfusion on the spot. I'm not saying that you don't know what happened but just please explain.

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: Well, he put a needle in the blood vessels, here, and there was a bottle there, I can't tell you whether it was an infusion or a transfusion. I'm not a doctor.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Yes. That's what I've asked you precisely. And my second question is this: In your statement on page 12 you say that you saw the rocket launcher. You said that you saw -- had seen it and that it fired a shot at the house. Today you said that there were six shots. And then in the statement, in the same paragraph, you said that you had heard shots coming from the direction of the police station. And you also told us that you had not served in the army. Can you describe a rocket launcher, or did it just seem to you that this was something similar to a rocket launcher? What is a rocket launcher? Where did you see it?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: Well, while they were shooting, you could see the fire that followed the whole line of shooting. I don't know what else to tell you. I have not been in the military.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: So you don't -- did not see the piece of artillery from which the shots came, you just saw the trace of fire; is that correct? Because if you had seen the rocket launcher you must have seen somebody at the rocket launcher, a person.

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: I explained, I think very clearly, that the police station could not be seen from where we were, but the shots came from the police station. So I repeat: The shots and the firing came from that area. Yes, from the police station.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: And I agree with you on that. But you could not see the piece that you refer to as a rocket launcher. You just think that this was a rocket launcher. I don't know how else to explain that because let's -- let me put it this way. If you heard something, that doesn't mean necessarily that you saw it, and if you did see it, then I would kindly ask you to describe a rocket launcher for us and what people are usually around it and if you just heard it, then that's that. Can you explain?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: Well, the firing against the Shaip Dema's house, I heard them and I thought the firing came from the police station. It could have been a rocket launcher, maybe a mortar. There was quite a big noise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Fila, we take the view that the witness did not see the weapon. If that helps you, let's move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Of course the witness himself says that. He confirms that he didn't see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: And the third question that I have is this: How far away is the Macedonian border from your house; or in terms of time, how long did it take you to get from your house to the Macedonian border?

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: From my house to Gjurgjedol we travelled for five hours. From Gjurgjedol to Blace, it took us ten to 15 hours, on foot.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Very well. And my final question: Why did it not occur to you to go to the clinic which is only half an hour away but instead you took your wife to Macedonia, which is 15 hours away? That's my last question.

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: Well, if the matters stood as you were describing them, the police would not have been shooting from the police station, and when they were shooting, how could we go in that direction? It was the police that were shooting towards us. It was a very dangerous situation, so we had to leave our homes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Maybe you didn't understand me. When you started moving towards the Macedonian border in a column, how come you did not go to the outpatients' clinic but you went to the Macedonian border? Nobody was shooting at you at the time. It doesn't make sense to me. And that is my last question, thank you.

utterances.speaker: ISA RAKA
utterances.text: [No interpretation].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: The answer hasn't been translated at the moment. Could you give that answer again, please, Mr. Raka?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [No interpretation].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I'm sorry to ask you to give the answer for a third time but there is still no interpretation. Someone is missing what you're saying.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can you hear me now? Sorry. It was very dangerous. It was very dangerous to go to the clinic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. O'Sullivan?

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: No questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And Mr. Visnjic?

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Ms. Kravetz?

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: I have no further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, Mr. Raka, that completes your evidence. Thank you very much for coming to the Tribunal to give it. And you're now free to leave.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCULLY
utterances.text: Your Honour, our next witness is Fadil Vishi. Mr. Vishi is a 92 bis (D) witness. The transcript from the Milosevic case is P2285, and there is an incorporated statement which is P2284. He'll be addressing events in the village of Dubrava which is still in the Kacanik municipality. The particular indictment paragraphs are 72(k), subsection (iv), and 75(k), subsection (iv), and as well as Schedule K the subsection of that relating to specifically to Dubrava. And Your Honour, I'm actually Mr. Scully, not Mr. Marcussen for the record. Although I'm sure he would do better.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: That statement, Mr. Scully is the 18th of October 1999, is it?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCULLY
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour, and there are no additional statements.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Vishi.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Would you please make the solemn declaration to tell the truth by reading aloud the document which will now be placed before you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Please be seated. Now, Mr. Vishi, we have before us the full written record of the evidence you gave in the trial of Slobodan Milosevic. We also have the statement you gave which was part of your evidence in that trial. So we've got a lot of information already in front of us that has been provided by you and we've all read it. The purpose of you being here is that so that you can answer particular questions that are asked by counsel representing the Prosecution and the various accused, and it's important in doing that that you concentrate on the particular question asked. There is no point in us going over the same information again that we already have in writing. The important thing for us is to try to supplement that. Obviously, everyone is going to ask you questions related to what we have in writing, but we hope to learn more by listening to what you have to say today and not simply to hear again what you've already told the Court. First person to ask you questions then will be for the Prosecution, Mr. Scully. Mr. Scully.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCULLY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCULLY
utterances.text: Could you state your name and spell your last name for the record, Mr. Vishi?

utterances.speaker: FADIL VISHI
utterances.text: My name is Fadil Vishi.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCULLY
utterances.text: And where do you currently live, Mr. Vishi?

utterances.speaker: FADIL VISHI
utterances.text: I live in the village of Dubrava in the municipality of Kacanik.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCULLY
utterances.text: And how long have you lived in Dubrava?

utterances.speaker: FADIL VISHI
utterances.text: I've been living in Dubrava from my birth.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCULLY
utterances.text: Did you provide a statement to the Office of the Prosecutor on 18 October 1999 which addresses events in Dubrava which took place in 1999?

utterances.speaker: FADIL VISHI
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCULLY
utterances.text: And did you also testify in the Milosevic trial regarding those same events?

utterances.speaker: FADIL VISHI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCULLY
utterances.text: Did you have an opportunity to review your October 1999 statement on 8 September of this year?

utterances.speaker: FADIL VISHI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCULLY
utterances.text: Bearing in mind the corrections you made to that statement during the Milosevic trial, is that statement otherwise correct?

utterances.speaker: FADIL VISHI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCULLY
utterances.text: Your Honours, my first substantive question relates to his statement at page 2 of the English and B/C/S as well as e-court pages 6 and 11 of the transcript which is P2285.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCULLY
utterances.text: Mr. Vishi, you've described how soldiers were stationed at the Silkapor factory and you've also described how soldiers would pass your village on the roads. Could you see what kind of uniforms those soldiers wore?

utterances.speaker: FADIL VISHI
utterances.text: The soldiers were wearing different kinds of uniforms but the ones that I saw myself had camouflage uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCULLY
utterances.text: Your Honour, the next question relates to the same pages.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCULLY
utterances.text: You've also described a day wherein Sylejman Gurri was seized by persons you described as soldiers. Could you see the uniforms the persons who took Sylejman Gurri were wearing?

utterances.speaker: FADIL VISHI
utterances.text: Yes. That's correct. I saw them with my own eyes, because I was very close.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCULLY
utterances.text: Was the uniform worn by the persons who took Sylejman Gurri the same type of uniform that was worn by the soldiers you saw around Dubrava?

utterances.speaker: FADIL VISHI
utterances.text: Yes, the same uniform, camouflage uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCULLY
utterances.text: May I have Exhibit 2306 at page 3 -- it's a photograph -- up on the screen? I believe that's page 1. May I have page 3?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCULLY
utterances.text: Directing your attention to the photograph that's on your screen, do you recognise the person that's in that photograph?

utterances.speaker: FADIL VISHI
utterances.text: Yes. I recognise him.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCULLY
utterances.text: Who is that?

utterances.speaker: FADIL VISHI
utterances.text: He is Sylejman Gurri, who, on the 5th of May, was kidnapped in my presence, and he was killed on the 25th of May. While this photograph was taken on the 26th of May.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCULLY
utterances.text: Were you present either when he was killed or when the photograph was taken?

utterances.speaker: FADIL VISHI
utterances.text: No, I wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCULLY
utterances.text: How do you know he was killed?

utterances.speaker: FADIL VISHI
utterances.text: Well, you can see from the photograph that he was killed. Somebody took this photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCULLY
utterances.text: Where did you get that photograph?

utterances.speaker: FADIL VISHI
utterances.text: I took this photograph from a person called Farid Vishi [phoen].

utterances.speaker: MR. SCULLY
utterances.text: And does that person live in Dubrava?

utterances.speaker: FADIL VISHI
utterances.text: No. He doesn't live now. But he used to live in the village of Nika. But he was married to somebody from my village.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCULLY
utterances.text: Was he in or around Dubrava in May of 1999?

utterances.speaker: FADIL VISHI
utterances.text: In May 1999, he was in his own village but his village is very close to mine. But the kidnapping happened in Dubrava.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCULLY
utterances.text: After you saw Sylejman Gurri kidnapped on the 5th of May, did you personally ever see him alive again?

utterances.speaker: FADIL VISHI
utterances.text: No. I didn't. I only saw this photograph where he is dead.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCULLY
utterances.text: Your Honours, the next question relates to statement page 3 in B/C/S and English. It's page 9 in Albanian.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCULLY
utterances.text: Mr. Vishi, in your statement you've described how on the 25th of May, 1999, soldiers surrounded Dubrava. Could you tell us what you mean by "surrounded"?

utterances.speaker: FADIL VISHI
utterances.text: I mean that on the 25th of May, at 3.30 in the morning, the whole village was surrounded by Serbian forces, military and paramilitary, and there was an offensive against the village that day. And there were other victims as well in addition to Sylejman Gurri.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCULLY
utterances.text: What kind of equipment did you observe the forces using?

utterances.speaker: FADIL VISHI
utterances.text: They had all kind of equipment, even heavy weapons, Pragas and APCs.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCULLY
utterances.text: How do you know what a Praga and an APC is?

utterances.speaker: FADIL VISHI
utterances.text: Well, I could tell because they are various kinds of military equipment.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCULLY
utterances.text: Had you seen that same equipment being used by Serbian military and police before?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would object to the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Just hold on, please, just now, Mr. Vishi. Yes, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Based upon the assertion of the police I read his statement and his testimony and he does not discuss the police, and since he's a 92 bis I would like to, you know, make sure that his testimony does not go out side the bounds of what was disclosed to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCULLY
utterances.text: I'll make it an "or," Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, "or" doesn't help.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yeah, I don't think it helps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Because the point that's being made is that there is no indication given in advance that this witness will say anything about the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCULLY
utterances.text: All right. I'll rephrase it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCULLY
utterances.text: Mr. Vishi, had you seen the soldiers who were around Dubrava using that same type of equipment before they surrounded Dubrava?

utterances.speaker: FADIL VISHI
utterances.text: We had seen them earlier, as well, because they were stationed at the Silkapor factory where such equipment -- where they used such equipment.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCULLY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCULLY
utterances.text: Your Honours, the next question relates to the following page in all languages. And may I have P2306, first page 7 up on the screen? It's another photograph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Just before you go on to that, have we to read a lot into this statement? Although -- I mean, you've asked a few questions which have advanced it somewhat but we have a situation of a village surrounded and we have movement from the village, and then we know about what happened to various people or we see what is said to have happened to various people. But what are we -- are we to read something into the suggestion that this was an offensive that involved Pragas and APCs, because they don't appear to have done anything according to the statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCULLY
utterances.text: I don't know of any additional evidence that this witness has. I'm certainly happy to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: No, no, no. I just want to be sure that I'm not missing the point of this. You've taken it as far as you understand it goes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCULLY
utterances.text: Yeah. And I'm happy to supply my interpretation, but I don't have any additional evidence.
